'''Marie S. Wilcox''' (died September 29, 1995) was an American high school mathematics teacher and textbook author who served as president of the [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]].

==Education and career==
Wilcox was a graduate of [[Indiana University Bloomington]],{{r|scholarship}} and taught mathematics at [[George Washington Community High School]] and [[Thomas Carr Howe Community High School]] in [[Indianapolis]] from 1927 until retiring in 1969.{{r|obit}} She served as president of the [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]] from 1954 to 1956.{{r|nctm}}

After retiring, she moved to Florida, where she died on September 29, 1995.{{r|obit}}

==Books==
Wilcox was the author or coauthor of textbooks in mathematics including:
*''Algebra, First Course'' (with John R. Mayor, Prentice-Hall, 1956){{r|a1c}}
*''Algebra, Second Course'' (with John R. Mayor, Prentice-Hall, 1957){{r|a2c}}
*''Mathematics, a Modern Approach'' (with John E. Yarnelle, Addison-Wesley, 1963){{r|mma}}
*''Basic Modern Mathematics'' (with John E. Yarnelle, Addison-Wesley, 1964){{r|bmm}}
*''Contemporary Algebra, First Course'' (with John R. Mayor, Prentice-Hall, 1965){{r|ca1c}}
*''Contemporary Algebra, Second Course'' (with John R. Mayor, Prentice-Hall, 1965){{r|ca2c}}
*''Mathematics, a Modern Approach, Second Course'' (Addison-Wesley, 1966){{r|mma2c}}
*''Basic Algebra'' (Addison-Wesley, 1977){{r|ba}}

==Recognition==
Wilcox was named a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1956.{{r|aaas}} An award for female mathematics students at Indiana University, the Marie S. Wilcox Scholarship, is named for Wilcox.{{r|scholarship}}
